text:
Maya: Quick sync  Polaris Systems asked for a joint bench next week focusing on perf/W at scale. They want node-level and per-GPU readings and a validated runbook we can both reference for the joint note.

Leo: Do we have their firmware/kernel constraints? Polaris mentioned a custom NVLink driver patch. That could affect kernel scheduling.

Polaris R&D Bot: Polaris note: NVLink patch v2.3 applied on test racks. Per-GPU sensors are enabled. Export format: CSV + JSON metadata.

Jordan: Ok. Two approaches: (A) run our harness in their env (preferred) or (B) we run same harness on our rigs and they mirror. (A) is better for reproducibility. We need a minimal container + shim and a signed IAM role for S3 upload.

Priya: Legal ask: we must not publish any numbers that include Polaris internal build IDs or IP. We'll request redaction of raw telemetry and only publish aggregated CSVs.

Maya: Actionable items: create runbook, agree on metric set, decide publishable configs, and prepare a short methodology paragraph. Also pick a single model for publishable numbers (recommendation: open-llm-7B-medium).

Leo: Metrics: avg_power_node(W), avg_power_gpu(W), tokens_per_sec, p95_latency(ms), tail_memusage(MB), kernel_launch_count. Also ambient_temp(C). Add a note about measurement window (exclude warmup 30s).

Jordan: Proposed publishable configs: "perf-max" (batch=8, seq=512), "efficiency" (batch=1, seq=1024, q4_nop). Keep quant names human-friendly.

Priya: I'll draft a short MSA addendum for publishing joint bench data and circulate to Polaris legal. Need to confirm whether per-GPU CSVs are allowed internally; if not, we only publish node-aggregates.

Maya: For kernel tuning knobs, suggest we sweep: threadblock_size (16/32/64), activation_tiling (compact/strided), and kernel_prefetch (on/off). Keep sweep small: 6-8 runs per config so not to overload racks.

R&D Bot: CI scheduling: can run sweep Monday-Wed in slots 02:00-06:00 UTC. Upload path s3://redwood-partner-polaris/1991234567/.

Leo: Reminder: ensure KV cache behavior is consistent. For efficiency runs we should enable prefix cache; for perf-max disable cache to measure raw throughput. Document that in methodology.

Alicia: Marketing note: Polaris wants a joint blog. We'll need two headline variations and a 200-word co-authored methodology section. Also request Polaris logo + brand guidelines.

Jordan: Small runbook excerpt to include in the container README:

```
# reproduce.sh
export REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=s3:partner-polaris
./run_bench --model open-llm-7B-medium --batch $BATCH --seq $SEQ \
  --sweep-file sweep.csv --warmup 30 --reps 3 --upload $UPLOAD_PATH
```

Maya: Good. Let's gate the public announcement on legal sign-off and on a 72-hour embargo after we've validated aggregated numbers.

Priya: Understood. I'll ask Polaris legal for a short statement on what they can waive for publication.

Leo: I'll prepare the sweep.csv template and a small script to normalize power units and timestamps.

R&D Bot: First slot reserved: Monday 02:30 UTC on polaris-ci-node-7. Notification on completion to this thread and #eng-runtime.

Jordan: If anyone is doing local dry-runs, use the "simulate-power" flag to avoid engaging PDUs.

Alicia: I'll draft the two headline options and the marketplace copy. Will wait for sample numbers to finalize claims.

Maya: Thanks all. Please post the docker image tag here when ready. Closing once the run completes and legal confirms publishable CSV scope.
